name: Operational Risk Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of operational risks across the organisation. The policy is owned by the Chief Risk Officer and applies to Risk, Operations, All Staff, and the Board. It is mandated by the PRA Rulebook (Pillar 2) and Basel III Operational Risk framework.
context: Regulatory Reference | PRA Rulebook (Pillar 2), Basel III Operational Risk

name: PRA Rulebook (Pillar 2)
description: Prudential Regulation Authority regulatory framework establishing capital and risk management requirements for operational risk. This is a primary regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's Operational Risk Policy.
context: Regulatory Reference | PRA Rulebook (Pillar 2), Basel III Operational Risk

name: Basel III Operational Risk
description: International banking regulatory standard establishing operational risk capital requirements and risk management principles. Forms part of the regulatory basis for FirstUK Bank's Operational Risk Policy.
context: Regulatory Reference | PRA Rulebook (Pillar 2), Basel III Operational Risk

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events. This is the primary risk category addressed by FirstUK Bank's Operational Risk Policy.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive role responsible for ownership and governance of the Operational Risk Policy at FirstUK Bank. The Chief Risk Officer has accountability for policy implementation, review, and effectiveness across the organisation.

name: All Staff
description: All employees of FirstUK Bank are identified as an audience for the Operational Risk Policy, indicating that operational risk management responsibilities apply across the entire organisation.
context: Audience | Risk, Operations, All Staff, Board

name: Board
description: The Board of FirstUK Bank is identified as an audience for the Operational Risk Policy, indicating Board-level accountability for operational risk governance and oversight.
context: Audience | Risk, Operations, All Staff, Board

context: FirstUK Bank maintains an Operational Risk Policy to identify, assess, and mitigate operational risks
operational risks (process failures, systems outages, fraud, compliance breaches, etc.) that could impact customers, staff, or business continuity

context: operational risks (process failures, systems outages, fraud, compliance breaches, etc.)

name: Systems Outage

context: operational risks (process failures, systems outages, fraud, compliance breaches, etc.)

name: Fraud

context: operational risks (process failures, systems outages, fraud, compliance breaches, etc.)

name: Compliance Breach

context: operational risks (process failures, systems outages, fraud, compliance breaches, etc.)

name: Operational Risk Management Policy
description: A formal policy establishing procedures for the bank's operational risk management framework. The policy mandates proactive identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, and reporting of operational risks to senior management and the Board.
context: To establish procedures for operational risk management that:
Report to senior management and Board

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk category that the policy is designed to address through proactive identification, assessment, and mitigation. Operational risk encompasses events and exposures that require monitoring and control to prevent adverse impact on the bank's operations.
context: To establish procedures for operational risk management

name: Proactive Operational Risk Identification
description: A mandatory requirement that the bank must identify operational risks proactively rather than reactively. This provision establishes the foundational obligation for the operational risk management framework.

name: Operational Risk Impact and Likelihood Assessment
description: A mandatory requirement to assess both the impact and likelihood of identified operational risks. This provision establishes the analytical obligation for evaluating the severity and probability of operational risk events.

name: Implementation of Operational Risk Mitigation Controls
description: A mandatory requirement to implement mitigation controls in response to identified and assessed operational risks. This provision establishes the obligation to deploy protective measures and safeguards.

name: Operational Risk Metrics Monitoring
description: A mandatory requirement to monitor operational risk metrics on an ongoing basis. This provision establishes the obligation for continuous surveillance and measurement of risk indicators.

name: Operational Risk Reporting to Senior Management and Board
description: A mandatory reporting obligation to communicate operational risk information, assessments, and metrics to senior management and the Board. This provision establishes the escalation and governance requirement for operational risk oversight.
context: Report to senior management and Board

name: Senior Management
description: Senior management holds accountability for receiving and acting upon operational risk reports and metrics. They are responsible for governance oversight of the operational risk management framework.
context: Report to senior management and Board

name: Board
description: The Board holds ultimate accountability for operational risk governance and receives reports on operational risk metrics, assessments, and mitigation activities. The Board provides strategic oversight of the operational risk management framework.
context: Report to senior management and Board

name: Enterprise-Wide Policy Framework
description: A foundational policy establishing universal applicability across all organizational dimensions. This policy mandates comprehensive coverage of business processes, systems, technology infrastructure, personnel, products, services, and all geographic locations without exception.

name: Universal Application to Business Processes
description: Mandatory requirement that the policy applies uniformly to all business processes conducted by the organization without exception or carve-out.

name: Universal Application to Systems and Technology
description: Mandatory requirement that the policy applies uniformly to all systems and technology infrastructure used by the organization.

name: Universal Application to Staff and Contractors
description: Mandatory requirement that the policy applies uniformly to all staff members and contractors engaged by the organization, regardless of employment status or tenure.

name: Universal Application to Products and Services
description: Mandatory requirement that the policy applies uniformly to all products and services offered or delivered by the organization.

name: Universal Application to Geographic Locations
description: Mandatory requirement that the policy applies uniformly across all geographic locations where the organization operates, with no territorial exemptions.

name: Operational Risk Management Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing the prevention, detection, and mitigation of operational risks. The policy establishes the bank's stance on managing process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events through a comprehensive control framework.
context: FirstUK Bank operates controls to prevent, detect, and mitigate operational risks
with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: Process Failure
description: A category of operational risk arising from failures in internal processes and procedures that could disrupt banking operations or customer service delivery.
context: with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: System Outage
description: A category of operational risk arising from failures or unavailability of critical banking systems and infrastructure that could prevent normal business operations.
context: with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: Fraud
description: A category of operational risk arising from fraudulent activities, including internal and external fraud schemes that could result in financial loss or reputational damage.
context: with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: Compliance Breach
description: A category of operational risk arising from failures to comply with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies that could result in regulatory sanctions or reputational harm.
context: with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: External Event
description: A category of operational risk arising from external events beyond the bank's direct control, such as natural disasters, market disruptions, or third-party failures that could impact banking operations.
context: with particular focus on process failures, system outages, fraud, compliance breaches, and external events

name: Operational Risk
description: Risk of loss arising from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events. This is the foundational risk category defined in the operational risk framework.
context: Operational Risk = Risk of loss due to inadequate/failed processes, people, systems, or external events.

name: Account Opening Error
description: Operational risk arising from errors or failures during the account opening process that may result in incorrect customer data, compliance gaps, or service delays.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Payment Processing Failure
description: Operational risk stemming from failures in the payment processing system that may result in delayed, incorrect, or failed customer transactions.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Reconciliation Error
description: Operational risk arising from errors in account reconciliation processes that may lead to discrepancies between recorded and actual account balances.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Fraud Detection Failure
description: Operational risk where fraud detection mechanisms fail to identify suspicious or fraudulent activity, allowing unauthorized transactions or account misuse to proceed undetected.
context: Process failures causing errors or delays

name: Standard Operating Procedure
description: Documented standard operating procedures established as a mitigation control to prevent process failures and ensure consistent, error-free execution of banking operations.

name: Staff Training
description: Mandatory training program for staff to reduce process errors and ensure proper execution of operational procedures across account opening, payment processing, and fraud detection.

name: Supervisory Review
description: Supervisory review control mechanism implemented to monitor and validate operational processes, identify errors, and ensure compliance with established procedures.

name: Process Automation
description: Automation of banking processes implemented where possible to reduce manual errors, improve processing speed, and enhance operational reliability.

name: System Outage
description: Risk of technology system failures that cause service disruption to customers and operations. System outages represent a critical operational threat requiring mitigation through redundancy and disaster recovery measures.

name: Data Corruption
description: Risk of data integrity compromise through system failures or technical errors. Data corruption threatens the accuracy and reliability of customer records and financial transactions.

name: Integration Failure
description: Risk of failure in system integration points that connect disparate banking systems and processes. Integration failures can disrupt transaction processing and data flow across the organization.

name: Security Breach
description: Risk of unauthorized access to systems or data resulting from technology vulnerabilities or security control failures. Security breaches threaten customer data confidentiality and system integrity.

name: System Redundancy and Backup
description: Operational safeguard requiring duplicate systems and backup infrastructure to ensure continuity of service in the event of primary system failure. System redundancy mitigates the impact of technology outages.

name: Disaster Recovery Planning
description: Operational safeguard requiring documented procedures and testing for recovery from major system failures or disasters. Disaster recovery planning ensures the bank can restore critical services and data within defined timeframes.

name: Change Management
description: Operational safeguard requiring controlled procedures for implementing changes to systems and infrastructure. Change management mitigates risks of unintended system failures or security vulnerabilities introduced through modifications.

name: Security Control
description: Operational safeguard encompassing technical and procedural measures to protect systems and data from unauthorized access and security breaches. Security controls are fundamental to mitigating information security risks.

name: Staff Error
description: Risk arising from unintentional mistakes by staff members in executing banking operations, including negligence and procedural failures that may result in policy violations or unauthorized transactions.

name: Staff Misconduct
description: Risk arising from intentional wrongdoing by staff members, including unauthorized transactions, policy violations, theft, and fraud committed by employees.

name: Unauthorized Transaction
description: Risk that staff may execute transactions without proper authorization or outside the scope of their delegated authority, representing a form of staff misconduct.

name: Internal Theft
description: Risk of theft or fraudulent activity perpetrated by bank staff members against the institution or its customers.

name: Staff Training and Awareness
description: Mandatory training and awareness program designed to educate staff on policies, procedures, and risk mitigation to prevent errors and misconduct.

name: Segregation of Duties
description: Operational control that separates critical functions among different staff members to prevent unauthorized or erroneous transactions and reduce the risk of fraud or misconduct.

name: Access Control
description: Technical and procedural safeguard that restricts staff access to systems, data, and functions based on role and authorization level to prevent unauthorized transactions and misconduct.

name: Monitoring and Audit
description: Ongoing surveillance and periodic review of staff activities and transactions to detect errors, policy violations, and misconduct.

name: KYC Failure
description: Risk arising from failure to properly execute Know Your Customer identity and address verification procedures, resulting in regulatory violation and potential financial crime exposure.

name: AML Violation
description: Risk of breaching Anti-Money Laundering obligations, including failure to screen customers, monitor transactions, or file Suspicious Activity Reports as required by regulation.

name: GDPR Breach
description: Risk of violating General Data Protection Regulation requirements regarding personal data processing, storage, security, and customer rights, resulting in regulatory sanction and reputational harm.

name: Reporting Error
description: Risk of inaccurate, incomplete, or late submission of mandatory regulatory reports, including SARs, transaction reports, or other compliance filings.

name: Compliance Policy and Procedure Framework
description: Documented policies and procedures designed to establish compliance standards, define roles and responsibilities, and provide operational guidance for staff to prevent regulatory violations.

name: Compliance Training
description: Mandatory training program delivered to staff to ensure understanding of compliance obligations, regulatory requirements, and internal policies related to KYC, AML, GDPR, and reporting.

name: Regular Audit
description: Periodic independent review and testing of compliance controls, policies, and procedures to identify gaps, weaknesses, and violations requiring remediation.

name: Regulatory Monitoring
description: Ongoing surveillance and tracking of regulatory changes, guidance updates, and enforcement actions to ensure the bank remains informed of evolving compliance obligations.

name: Customer Fraud
description: Risk of unauthorized transactions initiated by customers against their own accounts or other accounts. This includes fraudulent activity perpetrated by account holders or persons acting on their behalf.

name: Employee Fraud
description: Risk of fraudulent activity perpetrated by bank employees, including embezzlement and misappropriation of customer funds or bank assets.

name: Third-Party Fraud
description: Risk of fraudulent activity perpetrated by external third parties, including vendors and service providers engaged by the bank.

name: System Fraud
description: Risk of fraudulent activity involving manipulation of bank systems or data, including unauthorized alteration of records or system compromise.

name: Fraud Detection System
description: Automated system deployed to detect and identify fraudulent transactions and suspicious activity across customer accounts and bank operations.

name: Segregation of Duties
description: Operational control requiring the separation of critical functions and authorization responsibilities to prevent any single employee from executing fraudulent transactions without detection.

name: Whistleblower Procedure
description: Formal procedure enabling employees and third parties to report suspected fraud, misconduct, or policy violations through protected channels without fear of retaliation.

name: Fraud Investigation Protocol
description: Formal procedure governing the investigation, documentation, and escalation of suspected fraud incidents, including evidence preservation and reporting obligations.

name: Reputational Risk
description: Risk of reputational damage arising from customer complaints on social media, regulatory violations reported in press, system outages causing service disruption, and fraud or misconduct scandals. The document identifies this as a key risk requiring mitigation through service quality, regulatory compliance, incident response, and media management.

name: Service Quality Focus
description: Operational safeguard focused on maintaining high service quality standards as a mitigation measure against reputational damage from service failures and customer dissatisfaction.

name: Regulatory Compliance Control
description: Control measure ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements to mitigate reputational risk from regulatory violations and press coverage of non-compliance.

name: Incident Response Procedure
description: Operational safeguard establishing procedures for responding to incidents including system outages, fraud events, and misconduct to minimize reputational damage and service disruption.

name: Media Management
description: Control measure for managing media communications and public relations in response to potential reputational threats, regulatory violations, or fraud/misconduct incidents.

name: Natural Disaster
description: External risk event arising from natural disasters that are beyond the bank's control and may disrupt operations. The policy identifies natural disasters as a category of external risk requiring mitigation through business continuity planning.

name: Cyberattack
description: External security threat from cyberattacks that are beyond the bank's control. The policy identifies cyberattacks as a significant external risk requiring cybersecurity measures and mitigation.

name: Vendor Failure
description: External operational risk arising from the failure or non-performance of third-party vendors or service providers. The policy identifies vendor failures as an external risk requiring vendor management controls.

name: Regulatory Change
description: External risk arising from changes in regulatory requirements or the regulatory environment that are beyond the bank's control. The policy identifies regulatory changes as an external risk requiring regulatory monitoring.

name: Business Continuity Planning
description: Operational safeguard designed to mitigate external risks such as natural disasters and cyberattacks by ensuring the bank can maintain critical operations during disruptions. Business continuity planning is identified as a key mitigation control.

name: Cybersecurity Measures
description: Technical and operational safeguards implemented to protect against cyberattacks and information security risks. Cybersecurity measures are identified as a primary mitigation control for external cyber threats.

name: Vendor Management
description: Operational control framework for managing third-party vendor relationships and performance to mitigate the risk of vendor failures. Vendor management is identified as a key mitigation control for external operational risks.

name: Regulatory Monitoring
description: Ongoing monitoring and surveillance control to track changes in the regulatory environment and ensure timely compliance with new or amended regulatory requirements. Regulatory monitoring is identified as a mitigation control for regulatory change risk.

name: Risk Assessment Framework
description: A formal policy establishing the bank's continuous process for identifying, assessing, and registering operational risks across departments. The framework mandates annual risk assessments, process walk-throughs, incident trend analysis, regulatory change assessment, and external threat monitoring, with centralized documentation in a Risk Register.
context: Continuous Process: Annual risk assessment (by department), Process walk-throughs with management, Incident trend analysis, Regulatory change assessment, External threat monitoring
Risk Register: Centralized log of identified risks

name: Annual Risk Assessment by Department
description: A mandatory requirement that each department must conduct an annual risk assessment as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Process Walk-Throughs with Management
description: A mandatory requirement to conduct process walk-throughs with management as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Incident Trend Analysis
description: A mandatory requirement to perform incident trend analysis as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Regulatory Change Assessment
description: A mandatory requirement to assess regulatory changes as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: External Threat Monitoring
description: A mandatory requirement to monitor external threats as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Centralized Risk Register Maintenance
description: A mandatory requirement to maintain a centralized log of identified risks documenting risk ID, description, impact, likelihood, current and residual risk rating, and responsible party.
context: Risk Register: Centralized log of identified risks
Risk ID, description, impact, likelihood, Current and residual risk rating, Responsible party

name: Operational Risk
description: The category of operational risks that the bank identifies, assesses, and monitors through its Risk Assessment Framework, including risks arising from process failures, incidents, regulatory changes, and external threats.

name: Risk Register
description: A centralized control mechanism for documenting and tracking identified risks, including their ID, description, impact, likelihood, current and residual risk ratings, and responsible parties.
context: Risk Register: Centralized log of identified risks
Risk ID, description, impact, likelihood, Current and residual risk rating, Responsible party

name: Department Management
description: The role responsible for conducting annual risk assessments and participating in process walk-throughs as part of the continuous risk identification process.

name: Risk Owner
description: The role assigned accountability for each identified risk, as documented in the Risk Register.

name: Minimal Impact Risk
description: Risk events with minimal financial impact under £10,000, typically involving minor delays or low customer impact. Represents the lowest tier of the bank's impact assessment scale.
context: Score | Minimal | <£10k | Minor delay, low customer impact

name: Low Impact Risk
description: Risk events with low financial impact between £10,000 and £50,000, typically involving service disruption lasting less than one hour affecting a limited number of customers.
context: Score | Low | £10k–£50k | Service disruption <1 hour, few customers

name: Medium Impact Risk
description: Risk events with medium financial impact between £50,000 and £250,000, typically involving system outages lasting 1–4 hours affecting many customers.
context: Score | Medium | £50k–£250k | System outage 1–4 hours, many customers

name: High Impact Risk
description: Risk events with high financial impact between £250,000 and £1,000,000, typically involving regulatory breaches, significant financial loss, or reputational damage.
context: Score | High | £250k–£1M | Regulatory breach, significant loss, reputational

name: Critical Impact Risk
description: Risk events with critical financial impact exceeding £1,000,000, involving major breaches, substantial losses, or license risk to the institution.
context: Score | Critical | >£1M | Major breach, large loss, license risk

name: Rare Likelihood Risk
description: Risk events with rare likelihood, occurring less than once in 10 years. Represents theoretical or extremely improbable scenarios.
context: Score | Rare | <1 in 10 years | Asteroid impact (theoretically)

name: Unlikely Likelihood Risk
description: Risk events with unlikely likelihood, occurring once every 3–10 years. Includes major system failures and unexpected events.
context: Score | Unlikely | 1 in 3–10 years | Major system failure, unexpected event

name: Possible Likelihood Risk
description: Risk events with possible likelihood, occurring approximately once per year. Includes process errors and occasional system glitches.
context: Score | Possible | 1 per year | Process error, occasional system glitch

name: Likely Likelihood Risk
description: Risk events with likely likelihood, occurring multiple times per year. Includes fraud detection events and customer complaints.
context: Score | Likely | Multiple per year | Fraud detection, customer complaint

name: Very Likely Likelihood Risk
description: Risk events with very high likelihood, occurring monthly or more frequently. Includes daily transaction errors and system slowness.
context: Score | Very Likely | Monthly+ | Daily transaction errors, system slowness

name: Low Risk Rating
description: Risk events rated in the green zone (scores 1–5) representing low risk. These risks are accepted with standard controls in place.
context: Green (1–5): Low risk, accept, standard controls

name: Medium Risk Rating
description: Risk events rated in the yellow zone (scores 6–10) representing medium risk. These risks require monitoring and targeted controls.
context: Yellow (6–10): Medium risk, monitor, targeted controls

name: High Risk Rating
description: Risk events rated in the orange zone (scores 12–15) representing high risk. These risks require mitigation strategies and senior oversight.
context: Orange (12–15): High risk, mitigate, senior oversight

name: Critical Risk Rating
description: Risk events rated in the red zone (scores 16–25) representing critical risk. These risks demand urgent action and immediate mitigation.
context: Red (16–25): Critical, urgent action, immediate mitigation

name: Risk Assessment Process
description: A four-step operational risk management process that requires departments to identify potential risks, score them based on impact and likelihood, implement targeted controls to mitigate identified gaps, and continuously monitor key risk indicators with escalation protocols.

name: Risk Identification by Department
description: Departments are required to list and identify potential risks, including process failures, systems failures, and fraud scenarios as part of the initial risk assessment step.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Risk Scoring with Impact and Likelihood Assessment
description: The Risk Team and Department must jointly estimate impact and likelihood of identified risks, consider existing controls, and calculate residual risk as part of the scoring step.

name: Control Gap Identification and Mitigation Implementation
description: Departments must identify control gaps, implement targeted controls to address residual risks, and assign clear responsibility and timelines for mitigation actions.

name: Continuous Risk Monitoring and Escalation
description: Ongoing monitoring of key risk indicators is required, with controls adjusted as needed and escalation triggered if risk levels increase beyond acceptable thresholds.

name: Department
description: Departments are responsible for identifying potential risks, implementing targeted controls to mitigate gaps, and leading the mitigation step of the risk assessment process.

name: Risk Team
description: The Risk Team works jointly with departments to score identified risks by estimating impact and likelihood, considering existing controls, and calculating residual risk.

name: Key Risk Indicator Monitoring
description: A continuous monitoring mechanism that tracks key risk indicators to assess whether implemented controls remain effective and to identify when risk levels increase.

name: Process Failure
description: A type of operational risk identified during the risk assessment process where established procedures or workflows fail to execute as designed.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Systems Failure
description: A type of operational risk identified during the risk assessment process where technology systems or infrastructure fail or malfunction.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Fraud Scenario
description: A type of risk identified during the risk assessment process encompassing potential fraudulent activities or schemes that could affect the bank.
context: Assess process failures, systems, fraud scenarios

name: Control Framework Policy
description: A policy establishing a three-tiered control framework for risk management and compliance oversight. The framework assigns distinct responsibilities across frontline management, risk and compliance functions, and internal audit to ensure comprehensive risk identification, monitoring, and assurance.

name: Frontline Management Risk Responsibility
description: Frontline management, through department heads, is responsible for risk management at the operational level, including the establishment of operating procedures, daily monitoring activities, and immediate incident response.

name: Risk and Compliance Independent Monitoring
description: The Risk & Compliance function must conduct independent risk monitoring, control testing, and escalation procedures to provide oversight separate from frontline operations.

name: Internal Audit Independent Assurance
description: Internal Audit must provide independent assurance through control testing, audit reporting, and follow-up verification to validate the effectiveness of controls across the organization.

name: Department Head
description: Department heads are responsible for frontline risk management, including establishing and maintaining operating procedures, conducting daily monitoring, and responding immediately to incidents.

name: Risk and Compliance Function
description: The Risk & Compliance function operates as the second line of defense, responsible for developing risk policy and framework, conducting independent risk monitoring, performing control testing, and managing escalation procedures.

name: Internal Audit Function
description: Internal Audit serves as the third line of defense, providing independent assurance through control testing, audit reporting, and follow-up verification of control effectiveness.

name: Daily Monitoring
description: A frontline control measure requiring continuous daily monitoring of operations and risk indicators to enable early detection of issues and immediate response.

name: Control Testing
description: A control measure performed by both Risk & Compliance and Internal Audit functions to validate the design and operating effectiveness of controls across the organization.

name: Escalation Procedures
description: Formal procedures established by Risk & Compliance to escalate identified risks and control issues through appropriate governance channels for management decision-making.

name: Incident Response Protocol
description: A frontline control requiring immediate response to identified incidents to minimize impact and prevent recurrence.

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events. The control framework is designed to identify, monitor, and mitigate operational risks across all three lines of defense.

name: Incident Management Policy
description: A policy governing the identification, classification, and management of unplanned events that cause actual loss or regulatory breach. The policy establishes the framework for incident response and reporting obligations.
context: Incident = Unplanned event causing actual loss or regulatory breach

name: Unplanned Event
description: An unplanned event that causes actual loss or regulatory breach, forming the basis for incident classification and management under this policy.
context: Incident = Unplanned event causing actual loss or regulatory breach

name: Actual Loss
description: Financial or material loss resulting from an unplanned event, which triggers incident management and reporting obligations.
context: Incident = Unplanned event causing actual loss or regulatory breach

name: Regulatory Breach
description: A violation of regulatory requirements or obligations resulting from an unplanned event, which constitutes an incident requiring management and reporting.
context: Incident = Unplanned event causing actual loss or regulatory breach

name: Incident Reporting Policy
description: Policy governing the immediate reporting, escalation, and documentation of incidents within the bank. Defines mandatory actions for staff upon incident discovery, including manager notification, incident logging, and conditional escalation to Risk and Compliance teams based on financial impact and regulatory implications.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss
Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Immediate Manager Notification
description: Requires all staff to report incidents to their manager without delay upon discovery or awareness of an incident.

name: Incident Log Recording
description: Mandates that all incidents must be formally recorded in the incident log as part of the immediate response process.

name: Risk Team Escalation for High-Value Losses
description: Requires escalation to the Risk team when an incident results in financial loss exceeding £10,000.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss

name: Compliance Escalation for Regulatory Breaches
description: Mandates escalation to Compliance team when an incident constitutes or may constitute a regulatory breach.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Incident Information Capture
description: Requires capture and documentation of specific incident details including date, time, incident type, affected systems/processes, estimated impact, root cause (if known), and immediate containment steps.

name: Incident Log
description: A formal record-keeping mechanism for documenting all incidents reported within the bank, capturing standardized information for audit, investigation, and compliance purposes.

name: Manager
description: Line managers are responsible for receiving immediate incident reports from their staff and initiating the escalation process as required by policy.

name: Risk Team
description: The Risk team is responsible for receiving and investigating incidents involving financial losses exceeding £10,000.
context: Escalate to Risk team if >£10k loss

name: Compliance Team
description: The Compliance team is responsible for receiving and investigating incidents that constitute or may constitute regulatory breaches.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Operational Risk
description: The policy addresses operational risks including system failures, process breakdowns, and incidents that may result in financial loss or regulatory breach.

name: Regulatory Breach
description: The policy identifies regulatory breach as a trigger for immediate escalation to the Compliance team.
context: Escalate to Compliance if regulatory breach

name: Fraud Investigation Policy
description: Policy governing the investigation of fraud incidents across the bank, with tiered response timelines based on incident value and mandatory escalation procedures for high-value cases. Establishes investigation methodology including root cause analysis, lessons learned documentation, and corrective action requirements.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO
Investigation Elements: What happened (detailed timeline), Root cause analysis, Lessons learned, Corrective action, Prevention measures

name: Fraud Incident Investigation Timeframe for Low-Value Cases
description: Mandatory requirement that fraud incidents valued below £10,000 must be investigated and resolved within 5 business days of detection.

name: Fraud Incident Investigation Timeframe for Medium-Value Cases
description: Mandatory requirement that fraud incidents valued between £10,000 and £100,000 must be investigated and resolved within 2 business days of detection.

name: Fraud Incident Escalation for High-Value Cases
description: Mandatory requirement that fraud incidents exceeding £100,000 must be immediately escalated to the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Executive Officer for urgent attention and decision-making.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO

name: Detailed Timeline Documentation in Fraud Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement that all fraud investigations must document a detailed timeline of events establishing what happened during the incident.

name: Root Cause Analysis in Fraud Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement that all fraud investigations must include a comprehensive root cause analysis to identify the underlying factors that enabled the incident.

name: Lessons Learned Documentation in Fraud Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement that all fraud investigations must document lessons learned to capture insights and knowledge from the incident for organizational improvement.

name: Corrective Action Implementation in Fraud Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement that all fraud investigations must identify and implement corrective actions to address identified deficiencies and prevent recurrence.

name: Prevention Measures Development in Fraud Investigation
description: Mandatory requirement that all fraud investigations must establish prevention measures to mitigate the risk of similar incidents occurring in the future.

name: Fraud
description: Financial crime risk involving deceptive or dishonest conduct that results in unauthorized financial loss or gain. This policy addresses fraud incidents across all value ranges and establishes investigation and escalation protocols proportionate to incident severity.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving immediate escalation of high-value fraud incidents (exceeding £100,000) and participating in urgent response and decision-making.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving immediate escalation of high-value fraud incidents (exceeding £100,000) and participating in urgent response and decision-making.
context: Incidents >£100k: Immediate escalation to CRO + CEO

name: Fraud Investigation Process
description: Structured investigation process triggered by detection of fraud incidents, incorporating tiered response timelines, root cause analysis, lessons learned capture, corrective action implementation, and prevention measure development based on incident value.
context: Investigation Elements: What happened (detailed timeline), Root cause analysis, Lessons learned, Corrective action, Prevention measures

name: Incident Escalation Policy
description: A policy governing the escalation of financial incidents based on loss amount thresholds, defining reporting timelines and responsible parties at each escalation level. The policy establishes mandatory escalation triggers ranging from departmental reporting for losses under £1,000 to immediate board and regulatory notification for losses exceeding £100,000.

name: Escalation to Department Manager for Losses Under £1,000
description: Incidents resulting in losses below £1,000 must be escalated to the Department Manager with a report to Risk. This represents the lowest escalation threshold in the incident management framework.

name: Escalation to Risk Manager for Losses Between £1,000 and £10,000
description: Incidents resulting in losses between £1,000 and £10,000 must be escalated to the Risk Manager with a report to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

name: Escalation to CRO and CEO for Losses Between £10,000 and £100,000
description: Incidents resulting in losses between £10,000 and £100,000 must be escalated to both the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Executive Officer with a mandatory reporting timeline of 24 hours.

name: Escalation to Board and Regulators for Losses Exceeding £100,000
description: Incidents resulting in losses exceeding £100,000 must be escalated immediately to the Board and relevant regulators with concurrent regulatory notification. This represents the highest escalation level requiring immediate action.

name: Department Manager
description: The Department Manager is responsible for receiving and handling incident escalations for losses below £1,000, with an obligation to report to Risk.

name: Risk Manager
description: The Risk Manager is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £1,000 and £10,000 and ensuring reporting to the Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: The Chief Risk Officer is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £1,000 and £10,000 (within 1 day) and for losses between £10,000 and £100,000 (within 24 hours), and must escalate to the CEO and Board respectively.
context: £1k–£10k | Risk Manager | Report to CRO within 1 day

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for receiving incident escalations for losses between £10,000 and £100,000 within 24 hours and for losses exceeding £100,000 with immediate notification.

name: Board
description: The Board is responsible for receiving immediate notification of incidents resulting in losses exceeding £100,000 and for coordinating regulatory notification.

name: Financial Loss
description: Financial loss resulting from incidents is the primary risk category addressed by this escalation policy. The policy categorises risk severity by loss amount thresholds, triggering proportionate escalation and reporting obligations.

name: Key Risk Indicator
description: Early warning signals of emerging risk used to monitor and identify potential compliance, operational, or financial threats before they escalate into material incidents. KRIs serve as proactive monitoring mechanisms within the bank's risk management framework.
context: KRIs = Early warning signals of emerging risk

name: Account Opening Error
description: Operational risk relating to errors occurring during the account opening process. The policy establishes a target threshold of less than 0.5% error rate, with remediation through process review and staff retraining when exceeded.
context: Account opening errors | <0.5% | Review process, retrain staff

name: System Availability Failure
description: Operational risk of system downtime or unavailability affecting banking operations. The policy establishes a target of 99.8% availability, with investigation and remediation required when this threshold is not met.

name: Reconciliation Variance
description: Operational risk arising from discrepancies between recorded and actual account balances or transaction records. The policy establishes a daily variance threshold of less than £1,000, requiring investigation and correction when exceeded.

name: Fraud Detection Gap
description: Risk that fraudulent transactions or activities are not detected by the bank's fraud monitoring systems. The policy establishes a target detection rate of 97% or higher, with tuning of fraud rules and investigation of detection gaps when the target is not met.
context: Fraud detection rate | 97%+ | Tune fraud rules, investigate gaps

name: Compliance Violation
description: Risk of breaching regulatory or internal policy requirements. The policy establishes a zero-tolerance target for compliance violations, with immediate remediation required upon any occurrence.

name: Customer Complaint Volume
description: Operational and reputational risk arising from customer dissatisfaction and formal complaints. The policy establishes a target threshold of fewer than 2 complaints per 1,000 accounts, with root cause analysis required when exceeded.
context: Customer complaints | <2 per 1,000 accounts | Root cause analysis

name: Account Opening Process Review
description: Control measure requiring review of the account opening process when error rates exceed the 0.5% threshold. This is part of the operational KRI framework to identify and remediate systemic issues in account setup procedures.
context: Account opening errors | <0.5% | Review process, retrain staff

name: Staff Retraining on Account Opening
description: Control measure requiring staff retraining when account opening error rates exceed 0.5%. This addresses root causes of operational errors through targeted staff development.
context: Account opening errors | <0.5% | Review process, retrain staff

name: System Outage Investigation and Remediation
description: Control measure requiring investigation and remediation of system outages when availability falls below the 99.8% target. This ensures rapid response to service disruptions.

name: Reconciliation Variance Investigation
description: Control measure requiring investigation and correction of reconciliation variances exceeding £1,000 daily. This ensures accuracy of financial records and account balances.

name: Fraud Detection Rule Tuning
description: Control measure requiring adjustment and optimization of fraud detection rules when the fraud detection rate falls below 97%. This ensures the fraud monitoring system remains effective.
context: Fraud detection rate | 97%+ | Tune fraud rules, investigate gaps

name: Fraud Detection Gap Investigation
description: Control measure requiring investigation of undetected fraudulent transactions when the fraud detection rate falls below 97%. This identifies weaknesses in fraud monitoring coverage.
context: Fraud detection rate | 97%+ | Tune fraud rules, investigate gaps

name: Compliance Violation Remediation
description: Control measure requiring immediate remediation of any compliance violations. The policy establishes zero tolerance for breaches, with urgent corrective action mandated.

name: Customer Complaint Root Cause Analysis
description: Control measure requiring root cause analysis of customer complaints when the complaint rate exceeds 2 per 1,000 accounts. This identifies systemic issues affecting customer satisfaction.
context: Customer complaints | <2 per 1,000 accounts | Root cause analysis

name: Account Opening Error
description: Operational risk associated with errors occurring during the account opening process. The policy establishes a target error rate of less than 0.5% with monthly monitoring to ensure account opening quality and compliance.

name: Payment Processing Failure
description: Operational risk related to failed transactions in the payment processing workflow. The policy establishes a target failure rate of less than 0.1% with daily monitoring to maintain payment system reliability.

name: Fraud Detection False Positive
description: Risk of false fraud alerts generated by fraud detection systems. The policy establishes a target false positive rate of less than 2% with weekly monitoring to balance fraud prevention effectiveness against customer experience impact.
context: Fraud Detection | False positive rate | <2% | Weekly

name: AML Screening Delay
description: Compliance risk arising from delays in executing AML screening processes. The policy establishes a target screening delay of less than 2 hours with continuous monitoring to ensure timely sanctions and PEP list checks.
context: AML Screening | Screening delay | <2 hours | Continuous

name: Account Opening Error Rate Monitoring
description: Operational control that monitors the error rate during account opening processes on a monthly basis to detect and remediate quality issues. Target threshold is less than 0.5%.

name: Payment Processing Failure Monitoring
description: Operational control that monitors failed transactions in payment processing with daily frequency to identify and resolve payment system issues. Target threshold is less than 0.1%.

name: Fraud Detection False Positive Rate Monitoring
description: Operational control that monitors the false positive rate generated by fraud detection systems on a weekly basis to optimize detection accuracy. Target threshold is less than 2%.
context: Fraud Detection | False positive rate | <2% | Weekly

name: AML Screening Delay Monitoring
description: Operational control that continuously monitors the time taken to complete AML screening processes to ensure compliance with regulatory timelines. Target threshold is less than 2 hours.
context: AML Screening | Screening delay | <2 hours | Continuous

name: Risk Committee
description: A quarterly governance committee responsible for overseeing risk appetite, Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), incident management, and control effectiveness. The committee comprises the Chief Risk Officer, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Compliance Head, and Internal Audit representatives.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit
Agenda: Risk appetite, KRIs, incidents, control effectiveness

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive role responsible for risk governance and oversight. Serves as a member of the Risk Committee with accountability for risk management strategy and implementation.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Senior executive role with governance accountability. Participates in the Risk Committee to oversee organisational risk appetite and control effectiveness.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Chief Financial Officer
description: Financial leadership role with governance accountability. Serves on the Risk Committee to oversee financial risk, risk appetite, and control effectiveness.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Compliance Head
description: Compliance leadership role responsible for regulatory and compliance risk oversight. Participates in the Risk Committee to ensure control effectiveness and incident management.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Internal Audit
description: Internal audit function with independent oversight accountability. Participates in the Risk Committee to assess control effectiveness and provide assurance on risk management.
context: Members: CRO, CEO, CFO, Compliance Head, Internal Audit

name: Risk Appetite Oversight
description: Quarterly governance obligation requiring the Risk Committee to review and oversee the organisation's risk appetite framework and alignment with strategic objectives.
context: Agenda: Risk appetite, KRIs, incidents, control effectiveness

name: Key Risk Indicator Monitoring
description: Quarterly governance obligation requiring the Risk Committee to review Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to assess the organisation's risk profile and control performance.
context: Agenda: Risk appetite, KRIs, incidents, control effectiveness

name: Incident Review and Escalation
description: Quarterly governance obligation requiring the Risk Committee to review incidents and escalate material issues for organisational awareness and response.
context: Agenda: Risk appetite, KRIs, incidents, control effectiveness

name: Control Effectiveness Assessment
description: Quarterly governance obligation requiring the Risk Committee to evaluate the effectiveness of risk controls across the organisation.
context: Agenda: Risk appetite, KRIs, incidents, control effectiveness

name: Department Risk Owner
description: A role responsible for identifying risks within their department, implementing controls to mitigate those risks, monitoring Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), reporting findings to the Risk team, and escalating incidents as required.

name: Risk Team
description: The central risk function to which Department Risk Owners report findings, KRI monitoring results, and escalated incidents across the organization.

name: Key Risk Indicator Monitoring
description: An ongoing monitoring mechanism through which Department Risk Owners track and measure Key Risk Indicators to assess the effectiveness of risk controls and identify emerging risks within their area of responsibility.

name: Risk Control Implementation
description: The operational safeguard requiring Department Risk Owners to design, establish, and maintain controls within their department to mitigate identified risks.

name: Incident Escalation
description: A mandatory reporting mechanism requiring Department Risk Owners to escalate identified incidents to appropriate governance channels for investigation and remediation.

name: Risk Team
description: The Risk Team is responsible for maintaining the bank's risk framework, aggregating risk assessments across the organisation, monitoring emerging trends, reporting findings to the Board Risk Committee, and serving as the primary liaison with regulatory authorities on risk matters.

name: Board Risk Committee
description: The Board Risk Committee is the governance body to which the Risk Team reports risk assessments, trends, and findings for board-level oversight and decision-making.

name: Risk Appetite Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal risk appetite statement establishing a conservative risk posture with defined operational loss tolerances, compliance violation thresholds, and fraud loss limits. The policy sets quantified acceptance criteria for annual operational losses, major incidents, compliance breaches, and fraud events.

name: Annual Operational Loss Tolerance Limit
description: Establishes the maximum acceptable annual operational losses at less than £50,000, representing 0.15% of revenue. This provision sets a hard ceiling on operational loss acceptance within the bank's risk appetite framework.

name: Major Incident Frequency Tolerance
description: Limits the acceptable frequency of major incidents to fewer than one per year. This provision defines the bank's tolerance for significant operational or compliance events.

name: Compliance Violation Zero Tolerance
description: Establishes a zero-tolerance policy for compliance violations, indicating that no regulatory or policy breaches are acceptable under the bank's risk appetite framework.

name: Annual Fraud Loss Tolerance Limit
description: Sets the maximum acceptable annual fraud loss at less than £100,000. This provision defines the bank's tolerance threshold for fraud-related financial losses.

name: Operational Risk
description: Operational risk as defined in FirstUK Bank's risk appetite framework, encompassing losses arising from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events. The bank sets a tolerance threshold of less than £50,000 annually.

name: Compliance Risk
description: Compliance risk as defined in FirstUK Bank's risk appetite framework, representing the risk of regulatory or policy violations. The bank operates under a zero-tolerance policy for compliance breaches.

name: Fraud
description: Fraud risk as defined in FirstUK Bank's risk appetite framework, encompassing fraudulent activities resulting in financial loss. The bank sets a tolerance threshold of less than £100,000 annually.

name: Training and Awareness Policy
description: A policy establishing mandatory training and awareness requirements for bank staff across operational risk domains. The policy mandates differentiated training schedules based on role, with all staff receiving annual operational risk awareness, process owners attending quarterly workshops, and risk team members pursuing advanced training and certifications.
context: Risk team: Advanced training and certifications

name: Mandatory Annual Operational Risk Awareness Training for All Staff
description: A mandatory requirement that all staff members complete a 1-hour operational risk awareness training session on an annual basis. This provision establishes the baseline training obligation for the entire workforce.

name: Quarterly Risk Workshop Attendance for Process Owners
description: A mandatory requirement that process owners attend quarterly risk workshops to maintain and enhance their understanding of operational risk management. This provision establishes a more intensive training schedule for staff with process ownership responsibilities.

name: Advanced Training and Certifications for Risk Team
description: A mandatory requirement that risk team members pursue advanced training and professional certifications to maintain specialized expertise in operational risk management. This provision establishes the highest training standard for dedicated risk personnel.
context: Risk team: Advanced training and certifications

name: Operational Risk
description: The category of risk addressed by the training and awareness policy, encompassing operational failures, process breakdowns, and control deficiencies that the bank mitigates through staff training and awareness programs.

name: All Staff
description: The collective of all bank employees who are subject to mandatory annual operational risk awareness training. This role encompasses the entire workforce and establishes baseline compliance obligations for training participation.

name: Process Owner
description: A defined role responsible for managing specific business processes, with enhanced training obligations including quarterly risk workshop attendance. Process owners are accountable for understanding and mitigating operational risks within their domains.

name: Risk Team
description: A specialized team responsible for operational risk management across the bank, with the highest training obligations including advanced training and professional certifications. The risk team maintains expert-level knowledge of risk frameworks and controls.
context: Risk team: Advanced training and certifications

name: Operational Risk Policy
description: Policy governing internal and regulatory audit procedures, operational risk assessment, process control testing, and compliance with PRA Pillar 2 requirements. Establishes framework for annual operational risk assessment, KRI validation, and incident investigation sampling.

name: Annual Operational Risk Assessment
description: Mandatory requirement for the bank to conduct an annual operational risk assessment as part of internal audit procedures.

name: Process Control Testing
description: Mandatory requirement to perform process control testing as part of internal audit procedures to validate operational controls.

name: Key Risk Indicator Validation
description: Mandatory requirement to validate Key Risk Indicators (KRI) as part of internal audit procedures to monitor operational risk exposure.

name: Incident Investigation Sampling
description: Mandatory requirement to conduct sampling of incident investigations as part of internal audit procedures.

name: Pillar 2 Compliance Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to comply with Pillar 2 requirements as part of regulatory audit procedures.

name: Prudential Regulation Authority Periodic Operational Risk Review
description: Regulatory requirement for periodic operational risk reviews conducted by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) as part of supervisory oversight.

name: Pillar 2 Requirements
description: Regulatory framework establishing supervisory review and evaluation process requirements for operational risk management and capital adequacy.

name: Operational Risk
description: Risk category encompassing potential losses from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events. Addressed through annual assessment, process control testing, and KRI validation.

name: Process Control Testing
description: Control measure involving systematic testing of process controls to validate their effectiveness in mitigating operational risks.

name: Key Risk Indicator Monitoring
description: Control measure involving validation and monitoring of Key Risk Indicators to track operational risk exposure and trends.

name: Incident Investigation Sampling
description: Control measure involving sampling and review of incident investigations to identify patterns and control gaps.

name: Internal Audit Function
description: Organizational function responsible for conducting annual operational risk assessments, process control testing, KRI validation, and incident investigation sampling.

name: Risk Department
description: Organizational unit responsible for risk management and assessment activities within the bank. Referenced as a key stakeholder in policy documentation and incident tracking.

name: Risk Assessment Template
description: A standardized template document used for conducting and documenting risk assessments across the organization. Serves as a control measure for systematic risk evaluation.

name: Incident Log
description: A tracking mechanism for recording and monitoring incidents across the organization. Used to maintain audit trails and support incident management processes.

name: Business Continuity Plan
description: A formal policy document establishing procedures and protocols for maintaining business operations during disruptions or emergencies. Identified as BCP-001 in the document reference system.
